data.body:
Implemented as change https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1669 (commit be915ab89c, stacked on 1662).

PREMISE VERIFIED. _process_start_time reads only /proc/<pid>/stat and returns None on every OSError, so on macOS current_start is always None, the recycled-pid condition is unsatisfiable by construction, and the branch fell to return False with the 1h ceiling explicitly not applied. Unbounded wedge confirmed.

CHANGE. On the live-pid branch, when current_start is None the verdict is unqualified and now takes _mkdir_lock_age_exceeds_ceiling. Corroborated-live (both start times known and equal) still returns False and is never broken on a timer. Known-and-differing still reclaims immediately, independent of age. stamped=None with current known is unchanged.

SAFETY ARGUMENT (recorded, and it is what makes this conservative). _mkdir_lock_is_stale is only reachable from _acquire_mkdir, whose stated precondition is that the caller already holds the exclusive fcntl leg, held for the ENTIRE lifetime of the mkdir leg. A genuinely live owner inside its own hold would still hold that leg, so a reclaimer could not have acquired it and cannot reach this line. Arriving here is itself evidence the stamped owner let go: the ceiling can only fire on an orphan. NOT added: reclaiming on fcntl_held directly, which the same invariant would justify but which widens when a lock may be broken beyond the recorded direction. Left for a follow-up decision.

CONTRACT CHANGE, DELIBERATE. tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py had test_aged_live_pid_with_unknown_start_is_NOT_reclaimed_by_the_ceiling, which pinned the old behaviour and called it 'THE BOUNDARY ... research rec #6, deliberately NOT this change'. That is precisely the gap this bug closes, so the test is inverted with a docstring explaining why, and the module docstring's out-of-scope note updated. It now also asserts a FRESH unqualified-live stamp is still honoured, so the fix reads as adding a bound rather than making the lock instantly reclaimable.

SEAM SPLIT. lock.py was 798/800. Moved the owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster to src/rebar/_store/lock_owner.py along the existing call graph: lock.py 510 LOC, lock_owner.py 339 LOC, both inside 200-800, dependency one-way with no cycle.

MIGRATION FINDING worth recording. The plan called for repointing 12 patch sites and 42 attribute sites, which I did. That was not sufficient: lock.py's first cut used 'from lock_owner import <name>', creating a SECOND binding, so monkeypatch on lock_owner did not reach describe_lock_holder and test_describe_never_raises_on_an_unreadable_stamp failed. Fixed by having lock.py reach every moved name module-qualified (_owner.X), leaving exactly one binding. This is the same hazard class as the re-export shim the plan rejected, and is now pinned by test_lock_module_does_not_re_export_the_moved_private_names.

EVIDENCE. 4 new tests (true recycled-pid simulation with a reaped pid and _pid_alive forced True, both fresh-honoured and aged-reclaimed; known-differing-start immediate reclaim; owner-less dir bounded via a forced rmdir failure; the no-shim guard). tests/unit/test_lock_age_ceiling.py 10 passed. Full lock suite 76 passed. Wider -k 'lock or store or concur or txn or append': 765 passed, 4 skipped. make lint and make typecheck (510 files) clean.
